Executive Summary
The DevOps Master Course is consolidated as a fifteen-volume, beginner-to-master curriculum.

This handbook 
defines the canonical release structure, learning sequence, evidence model, completion rules, and package 
organization.

It is designed to make the course usable as a self-study program, team enablement program, 
interview-preparation track, or enterprise academy.

Release outcome: The curriculum content is complete through Volume 15.

The implementation package adds 
executable labs, assessments, capstone assets, progress tracking, quality controls, and a sustainable update 
process.

4. Learning Journey
1.
Read the chapter and summarize the architecture in your own words.
2.
Complete the associated lab in an isolated environment.
3.
Capture commands, outputs, diagrams, test results and cleanup evidence.
4.
Complete the knowledge and scenario assessment.
5.
Explain the design in an interview-style review.
6.
Record scores and evidence in the progress workbook.
7.
Advance only when the required acceptance threshold is met.

6. Evidence-First Completion Rules

A chapter is read when the learner can explain its architecture and failure modes.

A lab is complete only after functional validation, security review, failure recovery and cleanup.

A part is complete when knowledge, practical and interview scores each meet the threshold.

A volume is complete when all required parts are passed and the volume project is demonstrated.

Course graduation requires the final capstone, mastery portfolio and release-quality documentation.

9. Administration and Mentoring Model

Learner owns execution, evidence and reflection.

Reviewer validates reproducibility, safety and engineering judgment.

Mentor focuses on misconceptions, trade-offs and interview communication.

Course administrator maintains releases, errata, links and audit results.
10. Graduation Definition
Graduated learner: Can design, build, secure, observe, operate, troubleshoot and improve an enterprise 
delivery platform; can communicate decisions to engineers, security teams, management and executives; and 
can demonstrate the work through reproducible evidence.
